titre: Reporting your separation to the Caf
resume: Report the separation to the Caf de La Réunion so your entitlements are recalculated on your income alone, and choose who receives the benefits in shared residence (cerfa n° 14000).
aQuoiCaSert: After a separation, your benefits from the Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office), such as family allowances, housing benefit, the prime d'activité (in-work bonus) or the ASF (family support allowance), are recalculated without your ex-partner's income. Reporting the change quickly opens new entitlements and avoids having to repay overpayments. In shared residence, both parents must also tell the Caf who receives the benefits. In Réunion, family allowances are paid from the first child, which makes this choice important even with only one child.
quiEstConcerne: Any Caf beneficiary who separates, whether they were married, in a PACS (civil partnership) or living together.
The ex-partner who was not the beneficiary and must open their own file to receive benefits.
Parents with shared residence, who must choose the beneficiary.
aSavoir: Shared residence, if you agree: the parents name a single beneficiary for all benefits, or split the family allowances in half and name a single beneficiary for the other benefits.
Shared residence, if you disagree: each parent automatically receives a share of the family allowances. The other benefits go in full to the designated parent.
The choice can only be changed after one year, unless the child's residence changes. If you do nothing, it is renewed.

Only the family allowances are split. Paje (prestation d'accueil du jeune enfant, early childhood benefit), complément familial (family supplement), housing benefit, AEEH (disabled child education allowance), ASF and ARS (back-to-school allowance) go to the designated parent. Exception: since December 1, 2025, each parent can receive the complément de libre choix du mode de garde (CMG, childcare allowance) according to their own situation.

In the overseas departments, including Réunion, a family allowance is paid from a single dependent child (Cnaf, network letter LR-2026-051). The national page on shared residence does not cover this case: see "To be confirmed".

Child who lives with you with no child support paid by the other parent: you may be entitled to the family support allowance (see the guide entry "Family support allowance (ASF, allocation de soutien familial)").
Taxes: a single, divorced or separated parent who lives alone with their children ticks box T and gets an extra half share (demi-part) of tax allowance.

aConfirmer: The national page on shared residence states that a parent with only one child does not receive family allowances, a mainland France rule. In Réunion, they are paid from the first child: how they are shared with only one child is to be confirmed with the Caf de La Réunion.
The Caf may ask for proof of separation if you still live under the same roof: the type of proof accepted is to be confirmed with the Caf.
To be confirmed locally: addresses, opening hours and appointment booking at the Caf de La Réunion reception desks (the caf.fr website could not be read automatically).
